lengthNote: This is a rough guide only. Covering every bullet point well matters more than hitting a number.

markGuide.note: This is our own plain-English summary to guide feedback. It is not the official mark scheme.

L1: Lowest band: a few relevant ideas, but the answer is very short or drifts away from the task. Little sense of who it is for. The format is missing or unclear, and ideas are not grouped.
Middle band: covers the task, though one or more bullet points are thin. Tone and format mostly suit the reader. Some paragraphs, and some linking words such as "also" or "because".
Top band: covers every bullet point with relevant detail. Tone, words and format suit the audience and purpose. Clear opening, ideas in paragraphs, and a proper close.
L2: Lowest band: communicates some ideas with some clarity for the purpose and the reader. Format and paragraphs are used to some extent, with some linking words. A range of sentences is attempted, including some complex ones, with some accuracy. Vocabulary and tone are mostly suitable.

Middle band: communicates ideas reasonably clearly, with a suitable amount of detail and a suitable length. The format is right and paragraphs are mostly accurate, with ideas linked most of the time. A range of sentences, including complex ones, is used with general accuracy. Vocabulary is wide and the tone suits the reader.

Top band: communicates ideas with consistent clarity and uses detail effectively. The format is right, paragraphs are effective and ideas are linked clearly all the way through. A range of sentences, including complex ones, is used accurately and effectively. Vocabulary is extensive and the tone is right for the reader throughout.

L1: Lowest band: frequent errors make parts hard to follow. Full stops and capital letters are often missing. Common words are often misspelt.

Middle band: mostly accurate full stops and capital letters, with some question marks, exclamation marks, commas or possessive apostrophes used correctly. Common words mostly spelt correctly. Grammar mostly accurate, with occasional slips in tense or agreement.

Top band: full stops, capital letters, question marks, exclamation marks, commas and possessive apostrophes used accurately. Common and some less common words spelt correctly. Grammar accurate throughout, including tense and subject-verb agreement.
L2: Lowest band: some correct grammar (agreement, a range of tenses, articles) and some correct punctuation from a range (commas, colons, apostrophes, inverted commas). Spelling of everyday and specialist words is sometimes accurate.
Middle band: generally correct grammar and punctuation across a range (commas, colons, apostrophes, inverted commas), and generally accurate spelling, including some specialist words.
Top band: consistently correct grammar with only occasional lapses, a wide range of punctuation used correctly, and accurate spelling including specialist words.

missions.title: Volunteer for Panda Week
missions.context: Hollins Park Wildlife Centre is looking for young volunteers to help visitors during its Panda Week. Volunteers will hand out maps, help at the craft table and answer simple questions on the Bamboo Walk.
missions.audience: Sam Patel, the volunteer coordinator. You have never met Sam.
missions.purpose: To apply for a place as a Panda Week volunteer.
missions.instruction: Write an email to Sam Patel applying to be a volunteer.
bullets: why you would like to volunteer at Panda Week
the skills or experience you would bring
when you are available, and any questions you have
why you would like to volunteer at Panda Week
the skills or experience that make you a good choice, with examples
when you are available, and anything you would need to know before you start

missions.title: Review a day with the animals
missions.context: A wildlife website is collecting reviews from visitors. You recently visited a zoo, wildlife park or farm park. It can be a real place or one you make up.
missions.audience: People reading the website who are deciding whether to visit.
missions.purpose: To review your day out and help others decide.
missions.instruction: Write a review for the website.
bullets: where you went, what you saw and what was good about the visit
what could be better, and whether you would recommend it

missions.title: Ask about a desert trip
missions.context: Sunpath Small-Group Tours runs a five-day trip in Israel. It visits Tel Aviv on the coast, the Negev desert and the Dead Sea. You are planning to go with family or friends next year, but you need more information first.
missions.audience: The bookings team at Sunpath Small-Group Tours.
missions.purpose: To ask for information before booking.
missions.instruction: Write an email to the bookings team.
bullets: who would be travelling and when you would like to go
what you would like to know about the trip, such as food, travel or activities
any special needs your group has, and how you would like them to reply

missions.title: Food from another country
missions.context: A travel website for young people is running a series called "Taste the World". Each article introduces food from one country. You have been asked to write about food in Israel.
info: Falafel: fried balls made from chickpeas, often eaten in pitta bread with salad.
Hummus: a smooth dip made from chickpeas, tahini (sesame paste), lemon and garlic.
Shakshuka: eggs cooked in a spicy tomato and pepper sauce, often eaten for breakfast.
missions.audience: Young people who read the travel website.
missions.purpose: To inform readers and make them want to try the food.
missions.instruction: Write an article for the website. You can use the information above.
bullets: one or two dishes and what they are like
why trying local food is a good way to get to know a place, with a tip for young travellers trying new food

missions.title: Have your say on the 14 bus
missions.context: Vale of Fenn Council has changed the route of the number 14 bus. It no longer goes along Mill Lane, and it now stops at the new health centre. The council is asking passengers for feedback.
missions.audience: The transport team at Vale of Fenn Council.
missions.purpose: To give your views on the new route and suggest improvements.
missions.instruction: Write an email to the council's transport team.
bullets: how you use the bus and how the change affects you
what is good and what is not so good about the new route
what you think the council should do next

missions.title: Get on board
missions.context: Your college newsletter is running a "Green Travel Week". The editor wants an article that encourages students to use buses and trains more.
missions.purpose: To persuade students to try public transport.
missions.instruction: Write an article for the college newsletter.
bullets: the benefits of using buses and trains
worries students might have, and practical tips (such as tickets, timetables or apps) that could help

missions.title: Young people in villages and towns
missions.context: Your local youth council wants to know whether young people living in villages have the same chances as young people living in towns. They have asked you to write a short report.
missions.purpose: To give information and make recommendations.
missions.instruction: Write a report for the youth council.
bullets: what there is for young people in a village and in a town near you (real or imagined)
the problems young people in villages face, such as transport, jobs or things to do
your recommendations for making things fairer

missions.title: Town or village?
missions.context: A website for young people is asking readers to write blog posts on the question: "Town or village: where would you rather live?"
missions.audience: Young people who read the website.
missions.purpose: To share and explain your opinion.
missions.instruction: Write a blog post giving your view.
bullets: where you would rather live, what it would be like, and your reasons
what you would miss about the other kind of place
